To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) PNs can be used for the behavioural characterisation in object-oriented modelling; (2) PNs can also be used for the dynamic selection and re-programming of the object behaviour; (3) The use of a modified TTCN notation for message sequence encoding is very effective for the development of re-useable modules; (4) Our modelling approach is suitable for the development of networking protocols, especially those which require dynamic re-programming.

(i) the OO paradigm can be successfully applied in protocol design, (ii) the PN formalism provides the necessary abstraction level for protocol design, and (iii) the proposed ILC model is a useful tool for modelling protocol entities and their interaction with other protocol entities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of OO principles to the design of communication protocols, with the aim of facilitating re-use and dynamic change of behaviour in the implementation.
the development of a methodology for designing re-useable software objects, which can be utilsed in the development of networking protocols.
the development of a formal methodology for modelling and implementation of communication protocols, based on the principles of object-oriented design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the OO paradigm provides a powerful tool for the modelling and implementation of network protocols and the PN formalism is an effective tool for describing the dynamic aspects of the protocols.
the proposed approach to protocol modelling is both practical and useful.
the proposed approach is an important step in the direction of developing a methodology for the development of re-useable software components based on the object-oriented paradigm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ILC Model provides a generic framework to facilitate inter-layer communication among protocol entities.
we have demonstrated how a formal, OO approach can be utilised for the development of re-useable software components, with the potential to be applied to a range of communication protocols.
we propose a new methodology to develop networking protocols based on OO modelling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PNs are an ideal tool to model the dynamic behaviour of objects, which in turn, allows us to develop a generic object model that can be re-used for different protocols.
PNs are a very effective modelling tool for protocol design.
the OO paradigm, when used in conjunction with PNs, can be used as a powerful design tool for the construction of re-useable networking software modules.
